3	Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve high task success on manipulation benchmarks~\cite{brohan2023rt2, kim2024openvla, kim2025oft}, but behavioral safety does not follow. On SafeLIBERO Level~I~\cite{hu2025vlsa}, OpenVLA-7B reaches 87.8\% Task Success Rate but only 74.5\% Collision Avoidance Rate (CAR), with collision rates of 43--93\% on the three most constrained tasks.

5	Two active research threads address related but distinct aspects. The first enriches VLAs with auxiliary spatial prediction (occupancy grids, depth maps, point clouds)~\cite{li2026spatialforcing, yuan2025depthvla, wu2025spatialvla, liu2025occvla}. At least fifteen such methods have appeared in the past year~\cite{wu2026stvla, chen2026gstvla, tu2026sgvla, xiao2026stemvla, li2025pointvla, sun2025geovla, bhat20253dcavla, li2025qdepthvla, abouzeid2025geoaware, rao2026augvla3d, li2026corridorvla}, all reporting improved task success under the implicit assumption that spatial awareness yields safer behavior. The second targets VLA safety directly through runtime action filtering~\cite{hu2025vlsa, zhai2026cofreevla, raja2024ogmcbf} or constrained RL~\cite{zhang2025safevla}. These lines are disconnected: no spatial method evaluates collision avoidance, and no safety method examines spatial representations. A recent survey~\cite{li2026vlasafety} confirms this gap. \section{Conclusion}

We presented a factorial study of auxiliary spatial supervision during VLA fine-tuning, bridging the gap between spatial VLA methods and behavioral safety evaluation. The best configuration---detached gradients with LayerNorm---reliably outperforms the Vanilla baseline (CAR $0.802$ vs.\ $0.745$; Hedges' $g{=}1.89$, bootstrap 95\% CI for $\Delta$: $[0.025, 0.089]$). A $2{\times}2$ factorial reveals two additive mechanisms: gradient flow under BatchNorm is associated with reduced collision avoidance ($g{=}{-}0.78$); LayerNorm provides a 3.5--4.8\,pp safety advantage ($g{\approx}0.88$). The two protections are complementary ($\eta^2_\text{interaction}{<}0.01$). Spatial label content showed no detectable effect (observed under v1 codebase).

These results yield three actionable guidelines for practitioners adding auxiliary spatial heads to VLAs: (1)~do not allow auxiliary gradients to flow through shared encoders under BatchNorm---this is the sole configuration associated with safety below baseline; (2)~if gradient flow is desired for representation learning, switch to LayerNorm, which eliminates the safety vulnerability; (3)~no ground-truth spatial labels are needed---the auxiliary head can be discarded at inference, making this a zero-cost safety intervention. The factorial methodology itself is a contribution: the additive decomposition ($p_{\text{interaction}}{=}0.76$) could not have been established by single-factor ablations, the dominant approach in prior work.

More broadly, our findings challenge the implicit assumption in the spatial VLA literature that richer spatial representations automatically yield safer behavior. Safety is sensitive to optimization dynamics---normalization type and gradient routing---not spatial content. Future work should verify the running-statistics hypothesis directly, extend to full fine-tuning and other VLA architectures, and investigate whether the additive pattern holds on physical platforms beyond tabletop manipulation.
